tiers.name: Critical
tiers.summary: Failure puts life, animal or plant health, the environment or national infrastructure at risk, or stops a statutory duty with no workaround.
tiers.examples: Flood warnings, animal disease control, payments at statutory deadlines
tiers.support_hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

tiers.name: Important
tiers.summary: Failure causes significant harm to users, revenue or reputation, but a short outage can be managed with a workaround.
tiers.examples: Licensing and permitting services, grant applications

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.summary: Failure is an inconvenience. Users can wait or use another channel until the service returns.
tiers.examples: Information services, most internal staff tools

tiers.name: Low
tiers.summary: Short-lived, experimental or low-use services where failure has little impact.

questions: Could a failure put people, animals, plants or the environment at risk?
Does the service support a statutory duty or legal deadline?
How much money flows through it, and what happens if payments are late?
How many users depend on it, and is there another channel they could use?
Would an outage be reported in the media or raised in Parliament?

categories.name: Availability and resilience
categories.description: The service is there when users need it and recovers quickly when it fails.

requirements.title: Availability
requirements.requirement: The service is available to users for the target percentage of its supported hours, measured monthly, excluding planned maintenance announced 5 working days ahead.
requirements.verify: Synthetic monitoring of the main user journey; monthly availability report.

requirements.title: Recovery time objective
requirements.requirement: After a major failure, the service is restored within the recovery time objective.
requirements.verify: Disaster recovery test with a timed restore.

requirements.title: Recovery point objective
requirements.requirement: No more data is lost in a failure than the recovery point objective allows.
requirements.verify: Backup configuration review and point-in-time restore test.

requirements.title: No single point of failure
requirements.requirement: The service runs across at least two availability zones, with no single component whose failure stops the service.
requirements.verify: Architecture review and a zone failure test.

requirements.title: Graceful degradation
requirements.requirement: When a dependency fails, users are told what has happened and do not lose information they have entered.
requirements.verify: Dependency failure tests in the pipeline.

categories.name: Performance and capacity
categories.description: The service is fast enough for users and copes with expected peaks.

requirements.title: Page response time
requirements.requirement: 95% of page requests complete within 2 seconds, measured at the server, at expected peak load.
requirements.verify: Load test at peak volume before go-live and after significant change.

requirements.title: API response time
requirements.requirement: 95% of synchronous API calls complete within 500 milliseconds at expected peak load.
requirements.verify: Load test and production monitoring of latency percentiles.

requirements.title: Peak capacity
requirements.requirement: The service handles twice the highest expected peak (for example a scheme deadline or flood event) without failing.
requirements.verify: Load test at 2x forecast peak; autoscaling configuration review.

requirements.title: Low bandwidth
requirements.requirement: Core journeys are usable on a 3G connection, with page weight under 500KB excluding cached assets.
requirements.verify: Lighthouse or WebPageTest on a throttled connection.

categories.name: Security
categories.description: The service protects its users, data and Defra.

requirements.title: Threat model
requirements.requirement: A current threat model exists and is reviewed at every significant change and at least annually.
requirements.verify: Threat model in the repository or linked from it, with a review date.

requirements.title: Vulnerability remediation
requirements.requirement: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed within 14 days and high within 30 days, or a risk decision is recorded.
requirements.verify: Scanner reports and the risk register.

requirements.title: Independent security testing
requirements.requirement: An IT health check proportionate to risk is completed before go-live and after significant change.
requirements.verify: Health check report and remediation plan.

requirements.title: Encryption
requirements.requirement: All data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher and encrypted at rest.
requirements.verify: Configuration review and automated TLS checks.

requirements.title: Access control
requirements.requirement: Users and services have only the permissions they need, granted by role, and access is reviewed at least every 6 months.
requirements.verify: Role model documentation and access review records.

categories.name: Accessibility and usability
categories.description: Everyone who needs the service can use it.

requirements.title: WCAG 2.2 AA
requirements.requirement: The service meets WCAG 2.2 level AA and publishes an accessibility statement.
requirements.verify: Automated checks in the pipeline, manual testing with assistive technology and an accessibility audit before public beta.

requirements.title: Design system
requirements.requirement: Public-facing pages use GOV.UK Frontend components and patterns.
requirements.verify: Code review and service assessment.

requirements.title: Works without JavaScript
requirements.requirement: Core journeys can be completed with JavaScript unavailable.
requirements.verify: End-to-end tests run with JavaScript disabled.

requirements.title: Supported browsers and devices
requirements.requirement: The service works on the browsers and assistive technologies in the GOV.UK Service Manual's supported list.
requirements.verify: Cross-browser test results.

categories.name: Observability and supportability
categories.description: The service can be monitored, supported and fixed by people who did not build it.

requirements.title: Logging and tracing
requirements.requirement: Structured logs, metrics and traces with correlation ids are sent to the platform observability tooling.
requirements.verify: Dashboard and a traced request across service boundaries.

requirements.title: Alerting
requirements.requirement: Alerts on user-facing symptoms reach the support team within 5 minutes of a breach.
requirements.verify: Alert test during operational readiness review.

requirements.title: Runbooks
requirements.requirement: Runbooks cover deployment, rollback, restart, common failures and contacts.
requirements.verify: Runbook walkthrough with the support team before public beta.

categories.name: Maintainability and testability
categories.description: The service is cheap and safe to change.

requirements.title: Automated deployment
requirements.requirement: Every change reaches production through an automated pipeline, and any release can be rolled back.
requirements.verify: Pipeline configuration and a rollback demonstration.

requirements.title: Automated tests
requirements.requirement: Unit, integration and journey tests run on every change, and the main branch is always releasable.
requirements.verify: Pipeline results and coverage of critical journeys.

requirements.title: Supported runtimes and dependencies
requirements.requirement: Languages, frameworks and dependencies are on supported versions, with automated update pull requests.
requirements.verify: Dependency report.

requirements.title: Documentation
requirements.requirement: The repository explains how to run, test and deploy the service and links to its decision records.
requirements.verify: README and ADR log review.

categories.name: Interoperability
categories.description: The service works with the rest of Defra and its partners.

requirements.title: Documented APIs
requirements.requirement: APIs are described with OpenAPI or AsyncAPI and published to the API catalogue.
requirements.verify: Specification in the repository; catalogue entry.

requirements.title: Standard identifiers
requirements.requirement: Shared entities use the identifiers in Defra's data standards (such as SBI, CRN, CPH and UPRN).
requirements.verify: Data model review.

categories.name: Data and compliance
categories.description: Data is accurate, protected and kept for the right length of time.

requirements.title: Data protection
requirements.requirement: A DPIA is completed before personal data is processed, and personal data is minimised.
requirements.verify: Approved DPIA.

requirements.title: Retention and disposal
requirements.requirement: Data is retained and deleted automatically in line with Defra retention schedules.
requirements.verify: Retention configuration and a disposal test.

requirements.title: Data location
requirements.requirement: OFFICIAL data is stored in UK regions.
requirements.verify: Infrastructure configuration review.

requirements.title: Data quality
requirements.requirement: Data quality rules are defined for data that feeds payments, regulatory decisions or statistics, and are measured.
requirements.verify: Data quality dashboard.

categories.name: Sustainability
categories.description: The service uses no more energy and resources than it needs.

requirements.title: Right-sized and switched off
requirements.requirement: Non-production environments scale down out of hours, and production scales with demand.
requirements.verify: Scaling configuration and monthly cost and carbon report.

requirements.title: Carbon reporting
requirements.requirement: The service's cloud carbon footprint is reported alongside its cost.
requirements.verify: Cloud provider carbon report.
